title: terraform-ingress-switcher-nlb-alb-cutover-health-checks-and-graceful-rotation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Scope: Implement a Terraform module and migration tooling to perform graceful cutovers between existing internal NLB-backed endpoints and a new ALB-based ingress layer with TLS termination inside customer VPCs. The goal is an automated, observable blue/green switch that maintains connection draining, health-check safety, and predictable certificate rotation without traffic blips.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: (1) Terraform module with an idempotent apply path that can create ALB + target groups alongside existing NLBs; (2) safe cutover plan that supports canary traffic split and automated health gating; (3) health-check and prober suite that validates both TCP (NLB) and HTTP/HTTPS (ALB) semantics; (4) integration with cert rotation (ACM/KMS) and connection-draining windows configurable per customer; (5) detailed rollout playbook and rollback path.
- Non-goals: replacing customer-managed DNS automation or modifying application pods — this ticket only touches infra modules and cutover orchestration.

Design decisions to make:
1) Dual-provisioning model: Module should optionally create both NLB and ALB resources and expose outputs for target IPs and listener ARNs. This enables side-by-side validation before switching DNS or route53 records.
2) Cutover orchestration: Provide a terraform-driven "switcher" resource that toggles primary route target with optional canary percent and health gates. For customers that prefer zero-DNS-change, support internal route-table swap using cloud-router/ENI where available.
3) Health checks: ALB uses HTTP GET 200/2xx checks to a /_hc/infra endpoint; NLB uses TCP health check + app-level UDP/TCP prober. Module should include a lightweight lambda or probe job (container) that can be deployed to the VPC to validate end-to-end application behavior post-cutover.
4) Connection draining: Default drain timeout set to 300s with explicit terraform variable. Ensure target group deregistration delay is surfaced and tested across AZs.
5) TLS termination: ALB terminates TLS via ACM cert or imported cert ARN; expose hooks to KMS/HSM key references and cert rotation lifecycle. Document a cert swap workflow that avoids 503s.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module creates ALB + target groups in the same TF state as existing NLB resources without destroying NLB by default.
- A smoke test (terraform apply + smoke-runner) can validate 99% of paths: new ALB responds to /_hc/infra, KV cache warm path, and load-balanced session stickiness.
- Cutover resource supports: canary percentage, health-gate thresholds (success rate and latency), automated progressive traffic shift, and abort on regression.
- Rollback is a single terraform apply that restores previous routing and redeploys original target group weights.
- Observability: console dashboard link, CloudWatch/Prometheus exporters, and span tags to tie the cutover to request traces.

Implementation notes and tasks:
- Terraform module files: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, locals.tf, tests/ (terratest). Use the provider abstractions we use in other private modules (provider aliasing for cross-account).
- Add a new resource type "redwood_ingress_switcher" as a wrapper (terraform custom provider not required; use a module pattern + small lambda for orchestration). Keep stateful progression in a Dynamo table for idempotency.
- Prober: lightweight container (go) that performs layered checks (DNS resolution, TCP connect, TLS handshake, GET /_hc/infra, mutating test if i/o stable). Ship as image redwood/prober:v0.3.
- E2E tests: Graph of scenarios (single AZ, multi-AZ failover, connection-drain heavy sessions). Include chaos test for in-flight request preservation.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module and prober image to staging account, run terratest against staging VPC.
2) Smoke-run blue -> green with 10% canary and health-gate for 10 minutes.
3) If stable, ramp to 100% over 30 minutes.
4) Monitor metrics (5xx, p95 latency, connection reset) and abort on 3 consecutive threshold breaches.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should the module manage DNS records (route53) or leave DNS to customer automation? Proposal: make DNS optional and off by default; enable via a boolean and documented IAM needs.
- Use Lambda + Dynamo for orchestration or adopt a small controller running in customer's cluster? Lambda reduces operator footprint but complicates cross-account invocation.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket emphasizes a terraform-first cutover primitive (switcher) that can orchestrate progressive traffic shifts between NLB and ALB rather than purely emitting resources. It also introduces a reusable in-VPC prober image for deep health validation, which differs from previous tickets that focused on single-provision modules or LB healthchecks only.
